content: Representatives from commercial organizations are not permitted to be members of a WHO guideline group. The final draft of the guideline underwent peer review by four content experts who provided technical feedback. These peer reviewers were selected from various expert panels both within and outside WHO. The scope of the guideline, evidence appraisal, and decision-making process began with an initial set of questions, which were critical for formulating recommendations. These questions were drafted by technical staff from the Evidence and Programme Guidance Unit, Department of Nutrition for Health and Development, based on the policy and programmatic needs of Member States and their partners. The questions followed the PICO (Population, Intervention, Control, Outcomes) format and were reviewed and discussed by the WHO Steering Committee for Nutrition Guidelines Development and the guideline development group. Modifications were made as necessary. The group assigned importance to each outcome on a scale of 1 to 9, with 7–9 indicating critical importance, 4–6 indicating importance, and 1–3 indicating low importance. The final key questions and critical outcomes for decision-making were listed in PICO format. WHO staff, in collaboration with researchers from other institutions, summarized and appraised the evidence using the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions. To identify unpublished or ongoing studies, a standard procedure was followed, contacting over 10 international organizations working on micronutrient interventions. Additionally, the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP) hosted by WHO was systematically searched for ongoing trials. No language restrictions were applied during the search. Evidence summaries were prepared using the GRADE approach to assess the overall quality of evidence. GRADE considers study design, limitations in study conduct and analysis, consistency of results, directness of evidence, and precision of effect estimates. Both systematic reviews and GRADE evidence profiles for critical outcomes were used to draft the guideline. The draft recommendation was discussed by the WHO Steering Committee for Nutrition Guidelines Development and the guideline development group during a consultation held in February 2013 in Geneva, Switzerland. Members of the guideline development group voted on the strength of the recommendation, considering the intervention's desirable and undesirable effects, the quality of evidence, values and preferences in different settings, and the cost of available options. These aspects were openly discussed, and members recorded their primary considerations individually. The group aimed for full consensus, but when unanimous agreement was not achieved after the first round of voting, further deliberations and a second round of voting were conducted. Consensus was defined as two-thirds agreement. WHO staff and external technical experts involved in evidence collection and grading were not allowed to vote. The majority of voting members (10 out of 12) agreed on a conditional recommendation, while two members considered it a strong recommendation. Regarding the management of competing interests, all experts participating in WHO meetings were required to declare any relevant interests before their participation, as per WHO rules and processes. The responsible technical officer and relevant departments reviewed these declarations before finalizing the group composition and inviting members to meetings. All guideline development group members and meeting participants submitted a declaration of interests form and their curriculum vitae before each meeting. Participants acted in their individual capacity, not as institutional representatives, and verbally declared potential conflicts of interest at the start of each meeting. WHO's procedures for managing conflicts of interest were strictly followed, and no real or perceived conflicts of interest relevant to this guideline were identified. WHO will continue to monitor research developments in the area of iron supplementation for postpartum women. If the guideline requires updating or if concerns about its validity arise, the Department of Nutrition for Health and Development will coordinate the update following formal WHO procedures. As the guideline approaches its 10-year review period, the Department of Nutrition for Health and Development, in collaboration with internal partners, will conduct a search for new evidence.
